sections.markdown: Godrick the Grafted** is a Site of Grace in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The structure containing Stormveil Castle's throne room features an attached courtyard that serves as Godrick the Grafted's boss arena. It is a narrow, paved approach through a densely-filled graveyard. A slain dragon limply hangs from a pole, and Godrick seeks to graft its power.

If Godrick is defeated, Gatekeeper Gostoc moves here to stomp his face in the dirt. If Nepheli Loux, Warrior receives the ashes of the Stormhawk King, Kenneth Haight, Limgrave Heir identifies and can install her as the rightful Lord of Limgrave. Lord Godfrey—or Hoarah Loux, Warrior—earned the crown when he defeated the Stormhawk King in single combat long ago. Statues of Godfrey and Serosh still decorate the throne room.

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown:
The Godrick the Grafted site of grace is located in Stormveil Castle. It can be reached from the Secluded Cell site of grace and passing through the boss fog gate. The site of grace appears inside the at the center of the graveyard after defeating Godrick the Grafted.

By passing through Stormveil's throne room and unlocking a door, the player can reach Liurnia of the Lakes.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Grafting** is a concept in Elden Ring involving the attachment of severed body parts onto another living being.

It is a blending, melding, or merging of life. It is a way to gain another's power through the attachment of severed limbs. Even the body parts of trolls and dragons could be grafted.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: Grafting was an accursed, grotesque, and shameful act practiced by certain members of the Golden Lineage, scions of Queen Marika the Eternal, most notably Godefroy and Godrick the Grafted. Godrick's grafting of Tarnished reflected his desperate attempt to compensate for his diluted divine blood through the accumulation of stronger limbs. The spirits of those he grafted became chrysalids.

sections.markdown:

- Godrick the Grafted

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Spirit tuning can ease the suffering of those who were grafted. Grafting inflicts less suffering than the way in which the Dung Eater ensnares souls.
- Warhawks had their talons "grafted", or forcibly replaced with lightweight swords.

sections.markdown:

- The Revenger merged many blades together to forge the Grafted Blade Greatsword, which appears to reflect the same principle of accumulated strength through amalgamation.

 - Similar to how the damage boosts to spells from certain casting implements work, the Highland Axe only grants this boost while held in one of the active hands (left or right, the currently "shown" equipment). The other active piece of equipment can still be two-handed, as the other hand slot will still count as active in the meantime (so having a Highland Axe in the active left hand slot while two-handing a Greatsword in the right hand slot will still grant a damage boost to the Greatsword's War Cry skill.
 - Unlike many other such boosts, wielding two Highland Axes will not stack the boost and it will instead remain at 10%.
- This item is depicted on the Axe Talisman.

sections.markdown: Ivory Sickle** is a dagger found in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Location**: Village of the Albinaurics
- The Ivory Sickle is looted from a stone coffin atop a hill at the Village of the Albinaurics, located beneath the Moonlight Altar in southwestern Liurnia of the Lakes. The item is near Old Albus and the Village of the Albinaurics site of grace. Beware the Depraved Perfumer.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- While the skill, Quickstep, is rather generic for an innate, locked skill, it's still very useful for quicker traversal on surfaces that slow you down, like deep muck or water, and for getting around in combat aggressively.
 - Due to this weapon's mild Intelligence requirement and light weight, it allows for exploiting the fact that Quickstep costs 0 FP if the weapon's requirements aren't met and 8 out of 10 Origins won't do so by default (only the Astrologer and Prisoner meet them). While this heavily limits the skill's in-combat usage (decreases amount of i-frames from 15 to 5) it does make it ideal for traveling over slowing surfaces.
- Unusually for a weapon upgraded with Smithing Stones, this weapon cannot be buffed or have its affinity changed.
- Though its Dexterity-scaling is slightly stronger than its Intelligence-scaling it gains the most Attack Power from a hybrid Dexterity/Intelligence approach.
 - Though the description may give the impression that this is a Faith-scaling weapon, it has not association with that stat.
- Overall a somewhat awkward weapon when it comes to how to best use it. A pure Intelligence build would do better with any other dagger with a Magic affinity while a hybrid Dex/Int build would probably prefer the Glintstone Kris.
 - It does admittedly serve as a decent stand-in for the aforementioned Glintstone Kris before getting it since it requires defeating two specific bosses holding Great Runes while the Ivory Sickle can be gained without defeating any boss at all if Stormveil Castle is bypassed and is available a bit earlier than most Cold or Magic affinity Skills. It's also a decent off-hand weapon but is somewhat hampered by requiring the somewhat hard-to-get-enough-of regular Smithing Stones.
- All attacks ignore 50% of guarded damage negation, though the dagger's low original Attack Power may make it appear to be lower than that.
 - This applies to both the Physical damage and the Magic damage.
 - As a dagger it will bounce away when hitting Medium Shields and Greatshields which means the weapon should preferably be used two-handed when attacking against those so that the guard-piercing can be fully exploited.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.markdown:
- Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
- Cannot have its Affinity or Skill changed.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Knight Bernahl** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Residing in the Warmaster's Shack of Limgrave, **Knight Bernahl** (騎士ベルナール) is a tarnished merchant who sells a number of Ashes of War. Bernahl was once a Tarnished champion worthy of becoming a lord, until his Finger Maiden cast herself into the flames.

Should the Tarnished join the Volcano Manor, they'll meet again with Bernahl, but this time he'll introduce himself as "Recusant Bernahl" (背律者ベルナール). After assassinating the first targets commissioned by Tanith, Bernahl will invite the Tarnished to join him in his hunt of Vargram the Raging Wolf and Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm at the Fortified Manor of Leyndell, Royal Capital.

He will become as a summon against the Godskin Duo in Crumbling Farum Azula.

The Tarnished will come face to face with Bernahl one last time to the north of the Great Bridge in Crumbling Farum Azula, where the recusant will invade his former comrade.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.markdown:
1. Limgrave (Warmaster's Shack)
 - *(Optional)* Speaking to Bernahl unlocks the option to purchase Ashes of War from him, regardless of the answer to his question.
1. Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor)
 - Speaking with Tanith and selecting "**Join Volcano Manor**" to receive the Drawing-Room Key, Bernahl will relocate to the eastern quarter of the manor, where Rya the Scout is also found.
1. Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor)
 - After assassinating Old Knight Istvan, as commissioned in the first Letter from Volcano Manor, speaking to Bernahl unlocks the option to purchase the Ashes of War he used to sell in Limgrave and two new additions, Eruption and Assassin's Gambit.
1. Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor)
 - After assassinating Rileigh the Idle, as commissioned in the second Letter from Volcano Manor, speaking to Bernahl prompts him to give the Letter to Bernahl to the Tarnished, inviting him to join forces against Vargram the Raging Wolf and Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm at the Fortified Manor of Leyndell, Royal Capital.
1. Leyndell, Royal Capital (Fortified Manor, First Floor)
 - Interacting with the invasion sign before the corpse holding Alberich's Set allows the Tarnished to fight alongside Bernahl against Vargram and Wilhelm. This assassination will reward the Tarnished with Vargram's Raging Wolf Set.
1. Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor)
 - With the task fulfilled, returning to Bernahl prompts him to give Gelmir's Fury to the Tarnished. This will also unlock his summon sign in Crumbling Farum Azula.
1. Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor)
 - After defeating Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, exhausting Bernahl's dialogue triggers his departure from Volcano Manor. His shop will still be accessible via the "Sword of Bernahl" left on his chair.
1. Crumbling Farum Azula (Dragon Temple Transept)
 - *(Optional)* If the Tarnished and Bernahl hunted down Vargram and Wilhelm in Leyndell, the recusant's summon sign will appear outside the Dragon Temple, to aid his brother in arms against the Godskin Duo.
1. Crumbling Farum Azula (Besides the Great Bridge)
 - Following the path to the north from the Great Bridge, Bernhal will invade the Tarnished before the tower with the chest containing the Old Lord's Talisman. When defeated, he drops the Blasphemous Claw.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Irina of Morne** is an NPC character in Elden Ring. She is found on the Weeping Peninsula, south of the Bridge of Sacrifice.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Irina is the daughter of Edgar, castellan of Castle Morne. Her eyesight has been weak since birth, and she wears a blindfold around her eyes.

Irina lived in Castle Morne with her father, until the Misbegotten servants rebelled and overran the castle. Edgar secreted Irina out of the castle, however the Misbegotten pursued her and killed her companions.

Irina encounters a Tarnished at the Bridge of Sacrifice on the Weeping Peninsula, and petitions them to rescue her father from Castle Morne, handing them a letter to deliver to him.

The Tarnished travels to Castle Morne and passes the letter onto Edgar. Once the Leonine Misbegotten has been defeated, Edgar leaves the castle to reunite with his daughter, vowing to devote his remaining days to her. However, by the time he reaches her location, Irina is already dead. Edgar swears vengeance on those responsible for her death, setting him on a path that eventually leads to his corruption by the Flame of Frenzy.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.markdown:
1. Weeping Peninsula (near Bridge of Sacrifice)
 - Irina can be found sitting on a rock near the Bridge of Sacrifice. Talk to her and accept her request to receive Irina's Letter.
1. Castle Morne
 - Find Castellan Edgar in Castle Morne and hand him Irina's Letter, before defeating the Leonine Misbegotten.
1. Weeping Peninsula (near Bridge of Sacrifice)
 - Return to Irina after delivering the letter to find her corpse. If you defeated the Leonine Misbegotten, Edgar will also be here.
 - If you rested at a Site of Grace in Liurnia of the Lakes after receiving Irina's Letter, Irina will die even if you have not done the Castle Morne segment of the questline.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Irina can be killed; however, this will prematurely end her questline and prevent Lightseeker Hyetta from appearing.
- If Irina dies, her blood can be used to soak the Lord of Blood's Favor for White Mask Varré.
- Lightseeker Hyetta shares the same appearance and voice actor as Irina of Morne. She will only appear if Irina's questline has ended with her death at the hands of the Misbegotten. This suggests Hyetta is Irina, possibly after undergoing a resurrection or rebirth ritual similar to Shabriri.
- Irina attacks by casting a weak spell resembling Rejection.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Voice actor: 
- Lightseeker Hyetta had an additional quest stage at Bellum Church in the , but the dialogue and key item she gave were both cut from the game by the release. The context it provided offered insight into her transition from Irina of Morne and into the characters of Irina and Edgar. Hyetta gave Irina's Necklace after receiving the Fingerprint Grape, abandoning her long search for its owner. Irina carried the locket with her everywhere, a precious farewell gift from someone dear.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Jar-Bairn** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Jar-Bairn is a young Living Jar who lives in the secluded village of Jarburg in Liurnia of the Lakes. Like his uncle Alexander, he is a warrior jar, and strives to become a champion just like Alexander.

Presently, however, he is on the lookout for a new Potentate for the village. He meets the Tarnished when they pay a visit to Jarburg, but determines that they are not suited to be the new Potentate due to their rough hands. Nevertheless, he welcomes them to the village and invites them to come back and pick the flowers growing in the village whenever they want. He also warns the Tarnished of poachers who hunt and destroy other living jars.

Eventually, Jar-Bairn finds a new Potentate in Diallos Hoslow, a former Recusant who abandoned Volcano Manor after giving up on his path of revenge. Despite his disappointment that Diallos is not as strong as the Tarnished, he admires his smooth hands.

Not long after Diallos becomes Potentate, Jarburg is beset by poachers. Diallos defends the village and fights off the attackers, but many of the jars are broken and Diallos himself succumbs to his wounds. Jar-Bairn vows to become a warrior like Diallos, so that he can protect everybody. The Tarnished, having fought and defeated Alexander, offers the young jar his innards, which he uses to become even stronger, deciding to leave the village in search of glory, like his uncle.

sections.markdown:
1. Jarburg
 - Jar-Bairn can be found sitting in front of a house north-west of the Site of Grace. Exhaust his dialogue and decide whether or not to accept his request- the decision does not affect the rest of the questline. After resting at a Site of Grace, speak to him again to exhaust his new dialogue.
1. Jarburg
 - If you have met Alexander, Warrior Jar, Jar-Bairn will have new dialogue after you rest at a Site of Grace again.
1. Jarburg
 - After reloading the area, speak to him again to receive dialogue about poachers. This dialogue becomes available after Knight Diallos has arrived at Volcano Manor.
1. Jarburg
 - After Knight Diallos has left Volcano Manor, return to Jarburg and speak to Jar-Bairn again.
1. Jarburg
 - Reload the area six times and speak to Jar-Bairn near the middle of the village. Speak to Diallos and then reload the area and speak to Jar-Bairn once more.
1. Jarburg
 - After defeating Alexander, Warrior Jar in Crumbling Farum Azula, return to Jarburg and give Jar-Bairn Alexander's Innards. Reload the area, and speak to Jar-Bairn again to receive his final dialogue.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown: - Jar-Bairn was added to the game as part of Update 1.03. Prior to this, Diallos's questline did not have a conclusion and Alexander's Innards served no purpose.

sections.markdown: Imps** are Enemies in Elden Ring, Shadow of the Erdtree, and Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Commonly found in Catacombs across the Lands Between, Imps are small, green stone Golems crafted with glintstone implements by an ancient golem-maker. They served as enduring attendants to the Erdtree Burial Watchdogs, guarding the tombs of the honored dead. Imps wield forked weapons known as "imp's tongues," whose undulating blades inflict Blood Loss. Each Imp wears a distinctive stone mask bearing the visage of a beast, demon, or elder.

They cling to walls and ceilings, waiting to ambush the unwary, and often fight in groups where their small size and agility make them dangerous opponents. However, attacking an Imp with Crystal Darts disrupts its programming, causing it to turn on allies and attack indiscriminately.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Kenneth Haight** is an NPC in Elden Ring. He claims to be the next ruler of Limgrave but is in need of assistance as his fort has fallen.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Kenneth Haight** is a nobleman and claims to be next in line as the rightful ruler of Limgrave. He resided in a fort known as Fort Haight, and is known for his considerable largesse, at least by his own account. Godrick the Grafted assumed control of Limgrave following the Shattering, and at some point sent a knight commander to seize Fort Haight.

Driven out of his home, Kenneth began searching for adventurers who might help him restore control of his fort. He was stumbled upon by a Tarnished champion, and despite some reticence in accepting the help of a Tarnished, bid them to retake his fort in exchange for a handsome reward, while also sharing with them his exceedingly low opinion of Godrick.

Upon the Tarnished's success, a joyous Kenneth Haight grants them a reward and thanks them profusely. In addition, he offers them the opportunity to be knighted and enter into his service. He tells them to meet him as his fort, where the ceremony shall be held.

However, upon seeing the sorry state of his fort, Kenneth becomes maudlin. Believing that Limgrave cannot remain without a proper ruler, he dedicates himself to finding a true and stalwart Lord of the proper lineage as soon as possible. He apologizes to the Tarnished, telling them he now lacks the authority to lift them to knighthood.

After the death of Godrick, Kenneth eventually encounters a worthy lord; Nepheli Loux. Kenneth joins her in the throne room of Stormveil Castle to aid her in assuming the reins of the castle. When the Tarnished who had once aided him comes to visit, Kenneth tells him he intends to eventually return to his fort, where he can fulfill his old promise and raise them to knighthood at last.

He may or may not be a reference to the real-life role-playing game designer Kenneth Hite.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.markdown:
1. Limgrave (near Third Church of Marika)
 - Speak to Kenneth atop the ruin near the Third Church of Marika and agree to clear his fort.
1. Fort Haight
 - Kill the Godrick Knight in Fort Haight.
1. Limgrave (near Third Church of Marika)
 - Return to Kenneth and receive an Erdsteel Dagger. Accept his offer to make you a knight.
1. Fort Haight
 - Speak to Kenneth in Fort Haight.
1. Complete Nepheli Loux's questline.
1. Stormveil Castle
 - Speak to Kenneth in Stormveil Castle, in the throne room beyond the Godrick the Grafted Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Diallos Hoslow** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Diallos Hoslow is a scion of House Hoslow and the younger brother of Juno Hoslow. From a young age, Diallos was all talk and no trousers, with an inability to commit to action. As a result, Juno inherited the Hoslow legacy without resistance. Juno loved his brother dearly and showered him with adoration. Diallos, in turn, admired his brother, a mighty warrior who lived up to the bloody legacy of House Hoslow. Diallos aspired to be like his older brother, knowing that pursuing the bloody legacy of their house would break his brother's heart.

Diallos had a servant by the name of Lanya and the two were companions since childhood. At some point, the two set out on a journey in the Lands Between, but Diallos lost track of the fickle Lanya, and the two became separated. He made his way to Roundtable Hold where he implored the Hold's visitors to keep an eye out for Lanya.

Diallos eventually managed to track Lanya down to Liurnia of the Lakes, where he found her dead. He deduced that the recusants of the Volcano Manor were behind her death and swore vengeance upon them. He tracked them down to their hideout on Mt. Gelmir, but when the proprietor of the manor, Lady Tanith, offered him a place among them, flattering him by telling him he had the stuff of champions, Diallos abandoned his vengeance and decided to join the manor as a recusant.

Diallos pursued the path of a recusant, dirtying his hands time and again, but soon came to realize his folly. Having achieved nothing, he declared himself a complete fool, just as his brother had said, for abandoning the path of revenge and sullying the name of his house.

Diallos left the Volcano Manor and travelled to Jarburg, a settlement for Living Jars. Diallos became Jarburg's new "Potentate" and devoted himself to caring for the jars. Diallos was at peace with his new calling, feeling for the first time in his life that he was on the straight and narrow. The jars enjoyed his soft, silky hands, but they were disappointed by his apparent lack of strength and courage.

When Jarburg was invaded by jar-poachers, Diallos took up arms to defend his charges. He was mortally wounded in the battle, but managed to drive off the poachers and saved most of the jars. Diallos died at peace, having finally proven his worth to his dear jars and to himself.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.markdown:
1. Roundtable Hold
 - (Optional) Diallos can be found in Roundtable Hold upon the player's first visit. He will ask you to look out for his servant, Lanya, who has gone missing.
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Academy Gate Town)
 - Diallos will appear in Liurnia of the Lakes, northwest of the Academy Gate Town Site of Grace. Talk to him and exhaust his dialogue.
1. Roundtable Hold
 - Diallos will return to Roundtable Hold. Speak to him to learn the location of Volcano Manor.
1. Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor}
 - After joining the Recusants, Diallos will appear in the drawing room in Volcano Manor.
 - After defeating Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy or completing one of Tanith's requests, speak to Diallos again and exhaust his dialogue.
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Jarburg)
 - After progressing the Jar-Bairn's questline, Diallos will relocate to Jarburg in Liurnia of the Lakes.
 - After resting at a Site of Grace five times, return to Jarburg to find Diallos dying. Speak to him and then reload the area to obtain Diallos's Mask and Hoslow's Petal Whip.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood** is a hostile NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Juno Hoslow is Diallos' older brother and the head of their illustrious house.

A successful, stern and self-possessed man of a few words, Juno inherited the legacy of the Hoslow family to protect his inept brother, whom he loved dearly.

Despite drenching himself in blood time and time again, he refused the invitation to the Volcano Manor. Later, he became their target.

His sign can be found in the Mountaintops of the Giants, outside the Shack of the Lofty.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.markdown:
1. Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor)
 - After joining the Volcano Manor and eliminating Old Knight Istvan and Rileigh the Idle under Tanith's request, retrieve the Red Letter to unlock Juno Hoslow's invasion sign in the Mountaintops of the Giants.
 - With Rileigh dead, you can also talk to Recusant Bernahl to receive the Letter to Bernahl, offering you to join him in his hunt against Vargram the Raging Wolf and Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm in Leyndell, Royal Capital.
1. Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor)
 - Once Juno is disposed of, return to Tanith to receive the Taker's Cameo: she'll now offer to transport you to the Audience Pathway Site of Grace by selecting **See the Lord**.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown: - With the Red Letter in inventory, even if Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy is defeated prior to the invasion, abruptly concluding Tanith's questline, not only will the invasion sign still be available, but the reward will also be relocated in the spot where the Red Letter was retrieved.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Jarburg** is a Location in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
A peaceful village populated by Living Jars, secluded on the eastern coast of Liurnia of the Lakes. Jarburg is the home of Alexander, Warrior Jar, though he left to pursue his fate some time ago, vowing to never return. The villagers are in need of a Potentate to protect them from poachers.

Jarburg is difficult and dangerous to access. Located on a lower level south of Carian Study Hall, it can be reached by descending massive gravestones jutting from the side of eastern the cliff.

It contains a multitude of respawning flowers in gardens scattered around the area.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Imbued Sword Key** is a Key Item in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown:
- Unlocks the disabled Sending Gates of The Four Belfries.
- Each key is consumed upon use.

sections.heading: Sending Gates
sections.markdown:
- **Crumbling Lands**: Leads to an isolated section of Crumbling Farum Azula, where the Pearldrake Talisman is found.
- **Night Sky Unceasing**: Leads to an isolated section of Nokron, Eternal City, where the Mottled Necklace is found.
- **Precipice of Anticipation**: Leads back to the game's starting area, allowing a rematch with the Grafted Scion. Also contains Stormhawk Deenh, The Stormhawk King, and the corpse of the Tarnished's former Finger Maiden for progressing White Mask Varré's questline.
A fourth Sending Gate is found at the Fifth Belfry in the Realm of Shadow, located behind Castle Ensis, on a small island north of the Castle Ensis Checkpoint Site of Grace. This area is part of the Scadu Altus.
- This gate leads to a body of water in the southern Ancient Ruins of Rauh, where the Verdigris Discus is found.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
A total of **four** Imbued Sword Keys can be found per playthrough.

1. The Four Belfries: Found in a chest near the The Four Belfries Site of Grace.
1. Academy of Raya Lucaria: Located on the rooftop section of Raya Lucaria, northwest of the Debate Parlor Site of Grace.
1. Caelid: Found in a chest guarded by a Twinsage Scholar outside Sellia, Town of Sorcery, nearest the Sellia Under-Stair Site of Grace.
1. Castle Ensis: Found in a chest in a tower southwest of the Castle-Lord's Chamber Site of Grace. Take the lower western opening from the grace and use the elevator to reach it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Required for parts of Nepheli Loux and White Mask Varré's questlines.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Kindred of Rot**, also known as **pests**, are enemies in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Anthropomorphic, insectoid beings that emerged from the Swamp of Aeonia, they are forsaken servants and unwanted children of the new Goddess of Rot. They are commonly found in places blighted by Scarlet Rot, such as Caelid and the Grand Cloister.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Fully grown pests found in Rot-infested areas. They wield glaives made from hard, sharpened shell, and can fire web-like threads from a distance. If Scarlet Rot or Poison is utilised near them, they receive a buff.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Fully-grown pests found in Rot-infested areas around the ancient Rauh Ruins and the Church of the Bud. They are colored pink to signify they have been embraced by Romina, Saint of the Bud. They wield glaives made from hard, sharpened shell, and can fire Pest Threads and Pest-Thread Spears from a distance. If Scarlet Rot or Poison is utilised near them, they receive a buff.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The pests at the Sellia Crystal Tunnel pray toward a statue of a woman.
- The pests at the Grand Cloister in the Lake of Rot pray toward the Scorpion's Stinger.
- The scarlet pests at the Rauh Ruins pray before a large, ancient statue of a woman.
- The pests loyal to Romina in Realm of Shadow are red, while those abandoned by Malenia are pale.
